prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 1997 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and approach
- Build a fair, free, open society; spread power and opportunity; combine market economics with active, enabling government.
- Invest for the long term; widen opportunity; protect the environment; modernise politics; decentralise power.
- Costed programme with an “Annual Tax Contract” for transparency.

Education (flagship)
- Raise basic income tax by 1p to invest £2bn/year.
- Universal high‑quality early years for 3–4 year‑olds; smaller primary classes (max 30 within 5 years).
- Double school books/equipment funding in year one; £500m over 5 years for repairs.
- General Teaching Council; tougher support/exit for poor teaching; better inspection and discipline.
- Minimum Curriculum Entitlement replacing rigid National Curriculum.
- Lifelong learning: Individual Learning Accounts; fair income‑linked student repayments; oppose top‑up fees; credit‑based post‑14 system; link all schools to the internet.
- Workplace training: 2% remissible levy (exempt SMEs); expand youth training to 2 days/week equivalent.

Economy and enterprise
- Stability: independent UK Reserve Bank; adhere to fiscal “golden rule”; support euro entry if Maastricht criteria met and approved by referendum.
- Shift tax from jobs/goods to pollution; promote saving (new SAYE‑style schemes).
- Small business support (late‑payment interest right, cut red tape, seed capital, reform business rates).
- Regional Development Agencies; technology transfer; tourism partnerships.
- Workplace partnerships, profit‑sharing; adopt Social Chapter.
- Competition: stronger law; single utilities regulator; consumer ombudsmen; independent financial regulation.

Environment, energy, transport
- Embed green goals in all policy; carbon emissions cut target 30% from 1990 in 15 years.
- Tax shift: carbon tax phased in to cut VAT/employers’ NI; boost energy efficiency, renewables; no new nuclear subsidies; focus on decommissioning/waste.
- National home insulation to end fuel poverty; cut VAT on conservation materials.
- Transport: invest in public transport; enable urban road pricing; keep London Underground public with private finance for expansion; treble rail freight and double passengers by 2010; tighten Railtrack targets with clawback/reacquisition if persistent failure; incentivise smaller, efficient cars (lower VED; adjust fuel duty).

Homes, communities, crime
- Release council capital receipts; enable local borrowing for new homes; Mortgage Benefit for first‑time buyers; end rough sleeping by 2000; tougher action on empty/poor housing.
- 3,000 more police on the beat; cut paperwork; restorative justice; focus custody on serious/persistent offenders; overhaul CPS; victims’ rights; Royal Commission on drugs.
- Rural: CAP reform to countryside contracts; bolster services, housing, transport, post offices; protect countryside/fisheries. Urban: regeneration partnerships, public transport, community policing.

NHS and care
- Extra £540m/year (funded by closing NI loophole + 5p on cigarettes); recruit 10,000 nurses or 5,000 doctors; cap waits at 6 months in 3 years.
- Six‑month halt to finance‑led closures; end two‑tier GP fundholding; national inspectorate; free eye/dental checks; shift to prevention; ensure NHS dentistry access.
- Community care: Carer’s Benefit; national standards/charging guidance.

Constitution and rights
- Bill of Rights (ECHR in UK law); Human Rights Commission; Freedom of Information; cut quangos; referendums on major constitutional changes.
- Electoral reform (PR for all elections), reduce MPs by one‑third, fixed 4‑year terms, predominantly elected second chamber.
- Devolution: Scottish Parliament and Welsh Senedd (PR, tax powers); English regional assemblies where desired; stronger local government; move to Local Income Tax and fairer business rates.

Welfare, equality, opportunity
- Break poverty trap: raise tax thresholds; simplify benefits into Low Income Benefit; benefit‑to‑work transfers for long‑term unemployed; childcare strategy; regional minimum wage.
- Pensions: earnings‑linked top‑up for poorest; flexible retirement 60–70; citizenship‑based state pension; replace SERPS with universal personal/occupational schemes (preserve accrued rights).
- Women: equal pay/progression; fair pensions; NHS access; tackle violence.
- Disabled: comprehensive civil rights; Partial Capacity Benefit; accessibility code; SEN funding.
- Ethnic minorities: merged equalities commission; stronger anti‑discrimination; fair immigration/asylum.
- LGBT: equal age of consent; repeal Section 28; outlaw orientation‑based discrimination.
- Animal welfare: dog registration; curb live transport; ban testing for cosmetics/weapons/tobacco; free vote on hunting; ban snares; protect endangered species.

Foreign, defence, global issues
- Pro‑EU reform and enlargement; PR for MEPs; more majority voting with veto on core issues; join euro if criteria + referendum.
- Strong NATO‑based defence; retain Trident with capped warheads; pursue arms control.
- UN reform: stronger peacekeeping, ICC; lead on climate targets; move toward 0.7% aid/GNP in 10 years; strict arms export controls; ban landmines; fair trade with labour/environment standards.
